records.quote: First: Drawing a circle passing through a given point :
records.text: First: Drawing a circle passing through a given point :

records.quote: Given : A is a given point on the plane.
records.text: Given: A is a given point on the plane. R.T.P: Draw a circle passing through point A. Construction:

records.quote: Take any choosen point as M on the same plane.
records.claim: Construction step 1: take any chosen point as M on the same plane.

records.quote: State the tip of the compass at M and with an opening equalling MA
records.claim: Construction step 2: place the tip of the compass at M and with an opening equal to MA draw the circle M. The circle M passes through point A.

records.quote: State the tip of the compass at another point M1 and with an
records.claim: Construction step 3: place the tip of the compass at another point M₁ and with an opening equal to M₁A draw circle M₁. The circle M₁ passes through point A.

records.quote: Repeat the previous work and note :
records.claim: Construction step 4: repeat the previous work and note the following.

records.quote: M1, M2, M, M3 circles through A
records.caption: Four overlapping circles all passing through point A, with centres (pink dots) labelled M, M₁, M₂, M₃: M₁ pink circle top, M yellow circle right, M₂ small yellow/blue circle near A, M₃ large blue circle bottom. Positions read from figure; verify.

records.quote: For each choosen point (center of the circle) it is possible to draw a circle passing through point A.
records.claim: For each chosen point (center of the circle) it is possible to draw a circle passing through point A.

records.label: Think
records.quote: What are the number of points on the plane?
records.text: What are the number of points on the plane? What are the number of circles that can be drawn and pass through point A ?

records.label: Think
records.quote: If the radii of these circles are equal in length, where are their centers located ?
records.text: If the radii of these circles are equal in length, where are their centers located ?

records.quote: From the previous we deduce that:
records.text: From the previous we deduce that:

records.quote: An infinite number of circles can be drawn passing through
records.claim: An infinite number of circles can be drawn passing through a given point such as A.

records.quote: If the radii of these circles are equal in length then their centers
records.claim: If the radii of these circles are equal in length, then their centers are located on a congruent circle whose center is point A.

records.quote: A1 A2 A3 A
records.caption: Many circles all passing through point A, with centers labelled A1, A2, A3 on a green circle centered at A. Labels A, A1, A2, A3 read from the figure; verify.

records.label: Drill
records.quote: If L is a straight line on the plane; A is a given point where A ∈ L.
records.text: If L is a straight line on the plane; A is a given point where A ∈ L. Use the geometric tools and draw a circle passing through point A, with radius length 2 cm. How many circles can be drawn? (do not erase the arcs).

records.quote: Second: Drawing a circle passing through two given points:
records.text: Second: Drawing a circle passing through two given points:

records.quote: Given: A and B are two given points in the plane.
records.text: Given: A and B are two given points in the plane. R.T.P: Draw circle M passing through the two points A and B i.e AB is a chord in circle M.

records.quote: Construction:
records.text: Construction:

records.quote: Draw the straight segment AB.
records.claim: Draw the straight segment AB.

records.quote: Draw the straight line L, the axis of AB where L ∩ AB = {F}.
records.claim: Draw the straight line L, the axis of AB, where L ∩ AB = {F} (the center of the circle is on the axis of the chord AB).
records.notes: Intersection symbol printed garbled in the image.

records.quote: Take any chosen point M where M ∈ L, state the tip of the compass
records.claim: Take any chosen point M where M ∈ L, put the tip of the compass at M and with an opening equal to MA draw circle M; it passes through point B.

records.quote: State the tip of the compass at another point as M1 where M1 ∈ L
records.claim: Put the tip of the compass at another point M1 where M1 ∈ L, and with an opening equal to M1A draw circle M1; it passes through point B.

records.quote: Repeat the previous work and note :
records.claim: Repeat the previous work and note:

records.quote: M3 M1 M O M2 B A L
records.caption: Line L is vertical, the axis of segment AB (red, horizontal, B left, A right). Several circles through A and B with centers M, M1, M2, M3 on L; the red circle is centered at O/M. Right angle mark at the intersection. Labels read from figure; verify.

records.quote: For each chosen point E on the axis of AB (center of the circle)
records.claim: For each chosen point E on the axis of AB (center of the circle), it is possible to draw a circle passing through the two points A and B.

records.label: Think
records.quote: What is the number of points of the straight line L?
records.text: What is the number of points of the straight line L? What is the number of circles that can be drawn andpass through the two points A and B ?

records.label: Think
records.quote: What is the radius length of the smallest circle
records.text: What is the radius length of the smallest circle that can be drawn to pass through the two points A and B ?

records.label: Think
records.quote: Can two circles intersect at more than two points ?
records.text: Can two circles intersect at more than two points ?

records.quote: From the previous, we deduce that :
records.text: From the previous, we deduce that :

records.quote: An infinite number of circles can be drawn to pass through two given points like A and B.
records.claim: An infinite number of circles can be drawn to pass through two given points like A and B.

records.quote: The radius length of the smallest circle can be drawn in order to pass through the two points A and B is equal to
records.claim: The radius of the smallest circle that can be drawn to pass through the two points A and B equals half the length of AB.

records.quote: Two circles can not be intersected in more than two points.
records.claim: Two circles cannot intersect in more than two points.

records.quote: Third : Drawing a circle passing through three given points:
records.text: Third : Drawing a circle passing through three given points:

records.quote: Given: A, B and C are three given points on the plane.
records.text: Given: A, B and C are three given points on the plane. R.T.P: Draw circle M passing through the three points A, B and C.

records.quote: (figure: circle M with L1, L2, points A, B, C)
records.caption: Circle with centre M, passing through A, B and C. Line L1 (black, vertical with arrows) is the axis of AB and passes through M; line L2 (pink) is the axis of BC and passes through M. C is at top left, B at bottom left, A at bottom right of the circle. Right-angle marks and equal-length tick marks are shown on AB and BC.

records.quote: Construction:
records.claim: Construction:

records.quote: Draw the straight line L1 axis of AB thus M ∈ L1 .
records.claim: Draw the straight line $L_1$, the axis of $\overline{AB}$, thus $M \in L_1$.

records.quote: Draw the straight line L2 axis of BC thus M ∈ L2 .
records.claim: Draw the straight line $L_2$, the axis of $\overline{BC}$, thus $M \in L_2$.

records.quote: If L1 ∩ L2 = {M}, state the tip of the compass at point M
records.claim: If $L_1 \cap L_2 = \{M\}$, place the tip of the compass at point M with an opening equalling MA. Draw the circle M. You will find it passing through the two points B and C.

records.quote: If L1 ∩ L2 = φ , can you identify the position of point M ?
records.text: If $L_1 \cap L_2 = \phi$, can you identify the position of point M? Explain your answer.

records.quote: If A, B, and C are collinear then L1 // L2 and L1 ∩ L2 = φ
records.claim: If A, B and C are collinear then $L_1 \parallel L_2$ and $L_1 \cap L_2 = \phi$.

records.quote: A circle cannot be drawn passing through the three points A, B, and C.
records.claim: A circle cannot be drawn passing through the three points A, B and C (when collinear).

records.quote: (figure: collinear C, B, A with L2 and L1)
records.caption: Horizontal line through collinear points C, B, A (left to right) with tick marks showing equal segments; two parallel vertical lines L2 (axis of CB, between C and B) and L1 (axis of BA, between B and A) with right-angle marks, never meeting.

records.quote: From the previous, we deduce that :
records.text: From the previous, we deduce that :

records.quote: There is one and only one circle which passes through three noncollinear points.
records.claim: There is one and only one circle which passes through three noncollinear points.

records.label: Drill
records.quote: Using the geometric tools and draw the triangle A B C in which AB = 4 cm,
records.text: Using the geometric tools draw the triangle ABC in which AB = 4 cm, BC = 5 cm and CA = 6 cm. Draw circle passing through the points A, B and C. What is the kind of triangle ABC with respect to the measures of its angles? Where is the center of the circle located with respect to the triangle?

records.quote: Corollaries
records.text: Corollaries

records.quote: The circle which passes through the vertices of a triangle is called the circumcircle
records.label: Corollary
records.claim: The circle which passes through the vertices of a triangle is called the circumcircle of this triangle.

records.quote: a triangle is inscribed in a circle if its vertices are on the circle
records.claim: A triangle is said to be inscribed in a circle if its vertices are on the circle.

records.quote: The perpendicular bisectors of the sides of a triangle intersect
records.label: Corollary
records.claim: The perpendicular bisectors of the sides of a triangle intersect at a point which is the center of the circumcircle of the triangle.

objectives.label: Draw a circle through a given point
objectives.description: Draw circles passing through one given point by choosing any center, and recognise that infinitely many exist (equal radii give centers on a circle around the point).

objectives.label: Draw a circle through two given points
objectives.description: Draw circles through two points using centers on the axis (perpendicular bisector) of the chord, and know there are infinitely many, the smallest has radius half of AB, and two circles meet in at most two points.

objectives.label: Draw the circle through three points
objectives.description: Find the center as the intersection of the axes of two chords, draw the circle through three noncollinear points, and decide that collinear points give no circle.

objectives.label: Identify the circumcircle of a triangle
objectives.description: Use the circumcircle and inscribed triangle: its center is where the perpendicular bisectors of the sides meet.
